docs.title: money-printer-research
docs.text:
Collect, clean and model football match data from Understat and Transfermarkt.

The project builds one row per league match in the five big European leagues (England, Spain, Germany, Italy, France) from 2014/15 on, with the full-time result (home / draw / away) as the target and only pre-match features as inputs: Elo ratings, team and player fatigue, schedule congestion and each starter's form.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
make install               # uv sync --all-groups
uv run collect_data        # download the sources into data/
uv run clean_data          # write the cleaned tables and features to data/clean
uv run check_clean         # validate every clean CSV against its schema

docs.title: About This Project
docs.text: money-printer-research builds a match-outcome (home / draw / away) dataset for the five big European leagues and measures which pre-match features carry signal.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Understat: match schedule with goals and xG, and per-player match stats.
  • Transfermarkt (dcaribou/transfermarkt-datasets): every club's full calendar, including cups and European games, and the formations each side used.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Pre-match Elo ratings, team and player fatigue, schedule congestion (rest days, games in the last 7 and 14 days, European trips) and per-player form slots.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Every command is a console script declared in pyproject.toml under [project.scripts]. Run them with uv run <name>. They take no arguments; everything they read comes from the settings.

Command Entry point What it does collect_data data_collection.collect_data Download the Understat schedule, football-data.co.uk odds, Understat player stats and the Transfermarkt tables. See Collect. clean_data clean_data.exec_clean_data Clean the collected files and build the pre-match features; write nine CSVs. See Clean and Features. check_clean schema.check_clean Validate every CSV in the clean output folder against its schema. feature_importance analysis.exec_feature_importance Forward feature selection for the home / draw / away model on model_frame.csv, walk-forward by season. modeling analysis.exec_modeling Compare home / draw / away models on the selected features, check the baseline's calibration, score them on the held-out seasons, then save the logistic model. predict analysis.exec_predict H/D/A probabilities for every unplayed fixture in the schedule, from the saved model. backtest analysis.exec_backtest Bet the model's best-EV outcome against historical bookmaker odds, season by season, and report profit and ROI. notebook notebook.exec_notebook Open JupyterLab at the project root with the project's environment. show_config config.show_config Print the settings in effect and the file they came from. See Configuration. api api.exec_api Start the HTTP API. See Docker and API.

Entry points are imported only when called, so importing the package (for example money_printer_research.clean_data in a notebook) does not load the scraping libraries.

docs.title: collect_data
docs.text:
Runs the four collectors, fastest first:

  1. collect_schedule: one Understat request per league and season.
  2. collect_odds: one football-data.co.uk CSV per league and season, for backtest.
  3. collect_player_stats: one Understat page per match.
  4. collect_transfermarkt: one DuckDB download, then three Parquet exports.

A file that already exists is skipped, and a file is written only after it passes its raw schema check, so an interrupted or failed run can simply be started again. Failures for one league and season are printed as FAILED and the run carries on with the next.

docs.title: clean_data
docs.text: Runs clean, writes its four CSVs, then runs extract_features and writes five more. If a step fails, the command raises with that step's error; the clean CSVs stay on disk even when feature extraction fails.

docs.title: check_clean
docs.text:
Reads each CSV listed in schema.CLEAN_FILES with the dtypes of its schema (CSV loses some, such as season), validates it, and prints one line per file:

ok      match_leagues     123,456 rows
MISSING data/clean/players.csv
FAIL    elo: ...

Exits with status 1 if any file is missing or fails.

docs.title: feature_importance
docs.text: Reads model_frame.csv and selects feature groups for a multinomial logistic regression by greedy forward selection from Elo: each step adds the group that lowers the walk-forward log loss (seasons 2021 to 2023, each predicted by a model fitted on the seasons before it) the most, until no group gains MIN_GAIN. It then scores Elo alone, the selection and every group once on the held-out seasons from 2024, and says so if the selection differs from SELECTED.

docs.title: modeling
docs.text: Fits each model in analysis.modeling.MODELS on the SELECTED features, on the same walk-forward seasons, and prints log loss, ranked probability score, Brier score and accuracy; then the logistic baseline's calibration by probability decile; then every model once on the held-out seasons from 2024. Last, it refits the logistic model on every season and saves it with joblib to modeling.out_file (data/models/hda_logistic.joblib); analysis.modeling.load_model reads it back and its predict takes model_frame rows. joblib runs code from the file, so load only models you saved yourself.

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
Loads the model modeling saved and predicts every fixture the Understat schedule holds but has not seen played (is_result false), then writes game_id, date, league, both teams, p_H, p_D and p_A to modeling.predictions_file (data/predictions/upcoming.csv). Run modeling first.

Each fixture's features come from match_features.csv, using only what is known before kick-off:

  • Elo: each team's rating after its last played match; promoted teams start a new season the way clean_data starts them.
  • Games in the last 14 days: league games only (played ones and earlier fixtures), so a cup or European game in that window is missed.
  • Player slots: the line-up is unknown before kick-off, so a team gets the starters of its last played match and their values from then: the likely XI, one game old.

The schedule covers the seasons from understat.start_year up to, not including, understat.end_year. To predict the season in progress, set end_year past it (UNDERSTAT__END_YEAR=2027 for 2026-27) and run collect_data and clean_data. collect_data skips a schedule file that already holds every season, so delete data/raw/xg_schedule.csv to pick up newer results and fixtures.

docs.title: backtest
docs.text:
Reads the football-data.co.uk 1X2 odds collect_data downloaded to modeling.odds_dir, predicts every season from modeling.backtest_from with the logistic baseline fitted only on the seasons before it, and prices each game with Pinnacle's closing odds (falling back to Pinnacle's early price, the market average at closing, then Bet365's early price). Every other price in the files (all bookmakers, early and closing, Asian handicap and over/under 2.5) is available from analysis.odds.read_prices; see Bet schemas.

Each game's pick is the outcome with the highest expected value of a 1-unit stake, p * odds - 1. It prints the model's and the bookmaker's log loss and, for a few EV thresholds, the bets, hit rate, profit and ROI of betting every pick above it, and writes every game to modeling.backtest_file (data/predictions/backtest.csv). Needs data/clean/model_frame.csv, as modeling does, and the odds from collect_data. The web page at /backtest.html shows the same with a threshold slider.

football-data names teams differently from Understat; each name is matched to the team it shares the most match days with, so there is no alias list to keep.

docs.title: market_test
docs.text:
Can a model forecast results better than the betting market? Reads only the football-data.co.uk files collect_data downloaded (prices, results, shots on target), so it does not need the Understat pipeline.

It removes the bookmaker's margin from Pinnacle's early and closing 1X2 prices (proportional, power and Shin methods, compared), then scores five forecasters on every game from 2016/17, each season predicted only from the seasons before it:

Forecaster What it is early Pinnacle's early price, margin removed: what a bettor can act on close Pinnacle's closing price, margin removed market_refit The early price recalibrated by a logistic regression market_and_form The early price plus team form: Elo, recent goals and shots on target form_only Team form without the market

It prints each one's mean log loss and RPS, and for the pairs in market.COMPARISONS the mean per-game difference with a 95% interval. A model beats the market only if that interval is entirely below zero.

docs.title: strategies
docs.text:
Runs every strategy in strategies.toml (modeling.strategies_file), the pre-registered suite: written before any strategy was run, and changed only in commits that say so. It prints the commit of the file it ran with.

Each strategy is a rule for which bets to place at which price: back the favourite, always the draw, the model's best EV above a threshold, any price that beats Pinnacle's margin-free probability (line shopping), and so on, over 1X2, Asian handicap and over/under 2.5. Every bet is 1 unit, settled from the score; Asian handicap quarter lines split the stake.

For every variant (a strategy with one parameter value) and league it reports:

Column Meaning roi profit per unit staked, with its 95% interval close_ev expected profit per unit if Pinnacle's closing price is right: a far less noisy measure of edge than profit p_value, q_value one-sided test of ROI above zero, and the Benjamini-Hochberg q-value over every cell of the suite

and, per strategy, the ROI when each season uses the parameter value that made the most on the seasons before it.

Prices whose implied probabilities sum to under 0.97 (an arbitrage of 3% or more) are dropped as data errors, mostly in football-data's best-price columns.

docs.title: staking
docs.text:
Runs the strategy suite, then replays the bets of a few variants (staking.STAKED) in date order from a bankroll of 1 under each staking plan:

Plan Stake flat 1% of the starting bankroll kelly, half_kelly, quarter_kelly the Kelly fraction of the current bankroll, using the probability the strategy bets on, and half or a quarter of it martingale 1% of the start, doubled after each loss and reset after a win

A bankroll at 1% of its start is ruined and stops. It prints the history that happened (final bankroll, maximum drawdown, lowest point) and, over 1,000 resampled histories of 1, 3 and 5 seasons, the chance of losing half and 90% of the bankroll at some point.

docs.title: practicality
docs.text:
For the variants with a positive expected value at the closing price (line shopping), it prints:

  • how many seasons of betting it takes before an edge of that size shows as profit two standard errors above zero, and what it earns per season at 1 unit a bet
  • what is collected when soft bookmakers close each account once it is a few stakes up
  • the same rule on the Betfair exchange, which does not close winners, after commission

docs.title: report
docs.text:
Runs market_test, strategies, staking and practicality from the raw football-data files and writes one self-contained HTML page to modeling.report_file (data/report/report.html). The page:

  • answers whether any of it beats the market, in sentences built from the numbers
  • names the commit of the code and of strategies.toml it ran with, so the page can be rebuilt
  • holds every table and chart from those commands

The only hand-written text is the method and the limitations. It also writes the same results as JSON to modeling.analysis_file, which the API serves at GET /analysis and the /analysis.html page shows, with a league filter for the strategies.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Every path, league and season the pipeline uses is a typed setting in money_printer_research.config. Values are checked when they are loaded, so a typo or an impossible value stops the run with a message that names the setting instead of failing halfway through a scrape.

docs.title: Where values come from
docs.text:
Highest priority first:

  1. Arguments to Settings(...) or load_settings(...) (tests, notebooks).
  2. Environment variables. Join the section and the key with __: UNDERSTAT__START_YEAR=2018, CLEAN__OUT_DIR=/data/clean. Lists and tables take JSON: UNDERSTAT__LEAGUES='["ESP-La Liga"]'.
  3. A .env file in the working directory, with the same names as the environment variables.
  4. settings.toml.
  5. The defaults in config.py (shown in the tables below).

Sources are merged per key, so overriding UNDERSTAT__START_YEAR keeps every other [understat] value from settings.toml.

docs.title: Which settings.toml
docs.text:
• The file named by MPR_SETTINGS_FILE, if set. A missing file is an error.
  • Otherwise the first settings.toml found walking up from the working directory, then from the installed package.
  • Otherwise none: defaults and environment variables only.

Relative paths resolve against the folder that holds settings.toml (the project root), so uv run clean_data writes to the same place from any working directory. Absolute paths are used as they are.

To see the values in effect and the file they came from:

uv run show_config

docs.title: money_printer_research.analysis.feature_importance
docs.text:
Feature selection for the H/D/A model on model_frame.csv.

Features come from an explicit allowlist of groups (FEATURE_GROUPS), each built from a pre-match source; nothing outside it can reach the model, so the result of the match (goals, xG, is_result) cannot leak in. A group is one feature for both sides plus their difference, so a side is never kept without the other.

Selection is greedy and forward, by group, starting from Elo: add the group that lowers the walk-forward log loss most, until no group lowers it by MIN_GAIN. Walk-forward means each season in VALID_SEASONS is scored by a model fitted on the seasons before it only. The seasons from TEST_FROM on are touched once, at the end, to compare the selection with Elo alone and with every group.

The model is a multinomial logistic regression on standardised features, nulls filled with the training median: on this data it beats gradient-boosted trees, which overfit the few hundred games a feature's signal rests on.

docs.title: CLASSES = ['A', 'D', 'H'] module-attribute
docs.text: Sorted, the order of predict_proba's columns.

docs.title: FEATURE_GROUPS = {'elo': ['elo_home', 'elo_away', 'elo_diff'], 'league': [_league_column(lg) for lg in LEAGUES], 'fatigue': _sides('fatigue'), 'min_7d': _sides('min_7d'), **{s: _sides(s, diff=s not in ('prev_europe_away', 'next_is_europe')) for s in SCHEDULE}, 'formation': [f'{p}_{x}' for p in ('home', 'away') for x in ('defenders', 'midfielders', 'forwards', 'lines')], 'n_low_min': _sides('n_low_min', diff=False), **{f'player_{f}': _sides(f'{f}_mean') for f in PLAYER_SLOT_FEATURES}} module-attribute

docs.title: MIN_GAIN = 0.0005 module-attribute

docs.title: POST_MATCH = re.compile('^(full_time_.*|half_time_.*|(home|away)_(goals|xg)|tm_(home|away)_goals|is_result)$') module-attribute
docs.text: Known only after the match. No feature group may contain one (checked in load).

def columns(groups: list[str]) -> list[str]:

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def fit_score(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame, groups: list[str]) -> float:
    """Log loss on `test` of make_model fitted on `train` with the columns of `groups`."""
    cols = columns(groups)
    model = make_model().fit(train.select(cols).to_numpy(), train[TARGET].to_numpy())
    proba = model.predict_proba(test.select(cols).to_numpy())
    return float(log_loss(test[TARGET].to_numpy(), proba, labels=CLASSES))

docs.title: forward_selection(df, start=None, min_gain=MIN_GAIN, seasons=VALID_SEASONS)
docs.text:
Greedy forward selection by group; one row per step: the group added and the loss.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def forward_selection(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    start: list[str] | None = None,
    min_gain: float = MIN_GAIN,
    seasons: tuple[int, ...] = VALID_SEASONS,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Greedy forward selection by group; one row per step: the group added and the loss."""
    chosen = ["elo"] if start is None else list(start)
    best = walk_forward(df, chosen, seasons)
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"added": "+".join(chosen), "log_loss": best, "gain": None}]
    while rest := [g for g in FEATURE_GROUPS if g not in chosen]:
        scores = {g: walk_forward(df, [*chosen, g], seasons) for g in rest}
        group = min(scores, key=scores.__getitem__)
        if best - scores[group] < min_gain:
            break
        chosen.append(group)
        steps.append({"added": group, "log_loss": scores[group], "gain": best - scores[group]})
        best = scores[group]
    return pl.DataFrame(
        steps, schema={"added": pl.String, "log_loss": pl.Float64, "gain": pl.Float64}
    )

docs.title: held_out(df, candidates)
docs.text:
Log loss on the seasons from TEST_FROM of each candidate, fitted on the seasons before.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def held_out(df: pl.DataFrame, candidates: dict[str, list[str]]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Log loss on the seasons from TEST_FROM of each candidate, fitted on the seasons before."""
    season = pl.col("season_start")
    train, test = df.filter(season < TEST_FROM), df.filter(season >= TEST_FROM)
    rows = [{"features": "class prior", "log_loss": prior_score(train, test)}]
    rows += [{"features": n, "log_loss": fit_score(train, test, g)} for n, g in candidates.items()]
    return pl.DataFrame(rows)

docs.text:
model_frame.csv with the derived columns, every feature as Float64.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def load(path: Path) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """model_frame.csv with the derived columns, every feature as Float64."""
    df = with_derived(read_clean(path.parent, path.stem))
    feats = [c for cols in FEATURE_GROUPS.values() for c in cols]
    leaking = [c for c in feats if POST_MATCH.match(c)]
    assert not leaking, leaking
    return df.with_columns(pl.col(feats).cast(pl.Float64))

docs.title: main(path)
docs.text:
Print the forward selection, then the held-out comparison.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def main(path: Path) -> None:
    """Print the forward selection, then the held-out comparison."""
    df = load(path)
    print(f"{df.height} games, {len(FEATURE_GROUPS)} feature groups, test from {TEST_FROM}\n")
    steps = forward_selection(df.filter(pl.col("season_start") < TEST_FROM))
    chosen = [g for s in steps["added"] for g in s.split("+")]
    with pl.Config(float_precision=4):
        print("Forward selection, walk-forward log loss over", VALID_SEASONS)
        print(steps)
        print("\nHeld out:")
        print(
            held_out(df, {"elo": ["elo"], "selected": chosen, "every group": list(FEATURE_GROUPS)})
        )
    if chosen != SELECTED:
        print(f"\nselection differs from SELECTED: {chosen}")

def make_model() -> Pipeline:
    """Median fill, standardise, multinomial logistic regression."""
    return make_pipeline(
        SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000)

docs.title: prior_score(train, test)
docs.text:
Log loss of predicting every game with the training shares of A, D and H.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def prior_score(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Log loss of predicting every game with the training shares of A, D and H."""
    shares = [float((train[TARGET] == c).mean()) for c in CLASSES]  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
    return float(log_loss(test[TARGET].to_numpy(), [shares] * test.height, labels=CLASSES))

docs.title: walk_forward(df, groups, seasons=VALID_SEASONS)
docs.text:
Mean log loss over seasons, each scored by a model fitted on the seasons before it.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/feature_importance.py 
def walk_forward(
    df: pl.DataFrame, groups: list[str], seasons: tuple[int, ...] = VALID_SEASONS
) -> float:
    """Mean log loss over `seasons`, each scored by a model fitted on the seasons before it."""
    season = pl.col("season_start")
    return float(
        np.mean(
            [fit_score(df.filter(season < s), df.filter(season == s), groups) for s in seasons]
        )
    )

def with_derived(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add the derived columns FEATURE_GROUPS names: slot means, diffs, league flags.

    <f>_mean is the mean of a side's starter slots (nulls skipped), n_low_min the number
    of its starters under MIN_PREV_MIN previous minutes, <name>_diff home minus away.
    A diff whose h_/a_ columns are not in `df` is left out (predict's fixtures carry only
    the features the saved model uses); selecting it later fails loudly.
    """
    slots = {
        (s, f): [c for c in df.columns if re.fullmatch(rf"{s}_player\d+_{f}", c)]
        for s in ("h", "a")
        for f in PLAYER_SLOT_FEATURES
    }
    df = df.with_columns(
        *((pl.col("league") == lg).cast(pl.Int8).alias(_league_column(lg)) for lg in LEAGUES),
        *(pl.mean_horizontal(cols).alias(f"{s}_{f}_mean") for (s, f), cols in slots.items()),
        *(
            pl.sum_horizontal(pl.col(c).is_null() for c in slots[s, "xg90"]).alias(
                f"{s}_n_low_min"
            )
            for s in ("h", "a")
        ),
    )
    diffs = {
        c.removesuffix("_diff")
        for cols in FEATURE_GROUPS.values()
        for c in cols
        if c.endswith("_diff")
    }
    present = [n for n in sorted(diffs - {"elo"}) if {f"h_{n}", f"a_{n}"} <= set(df.columns)]
    return df.with_columns(
        (pl.col(f"h_{n}") - pl.col(f"a_{n}")).alias(f"{n}_diff") for n in present
    )

docs.text:
H/D/A models on the selected features (feature_importance.SELECTED), compared and checked.

Every model is fitted and scored the way feature selection was: walk-forward over VALID_SEASONS (each season predicted by a model fitted on the seasons before it), and once on the held-out seasons from TEST_FROM, fitted on everything before.

The baseline is feature_importance.make_model, a multinomial logistic regression. It is compared with the same model recalibrated (sigmoid, 5-fold on the training seasons), gradient-boosted trees, and a goals model: one Poisson regression per side for the number of goals, turned into H/D/A by summing the independent score grid.

Scores are log loss (what selection minimised), the ranked probability score (the usual one for football: it treats H, D, A as ordered, so calling a home win a draw costs less than calling it an away win), the multiclass Brier score and accuracy. calibration bins each class's predicted probability by decile and compares it with how often it happened.

After the comparison, fit_final refits the logistic baseline on every season (the held-out ones too: they have been scored, and the newest games matter most) and save_model writes it with joblib to settings.modeling.out_file. load_model reads it back; SavedModel.predict takes model_frame rows and returns P(A), P(D), P(H) per game. uv run modeling then writes the learning curve (analysis.learning_curve).

def calibration(y: np.ndarray, proba: np.ndarray, bins: int = 10) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Per class and probability decile: games, mean predicted probability, observed rate."""
    frames = []
    for i, c in enumerate(CLASSES):
        p = proba[:, i]
        edges = np.quantile(p, np.linspace(0, 1, bins + 1))
        frames.append(
            pl.DataFrame(
                {
                    "class": c,
                    "bin": np.clip(np.searchsorted(edges, p, side="right") - 1, 0, bins - 1),
                    "predicted": p,
                    "observed": (y == c).astype(float),
                }
            )
        )
    return (
        pl.concat(frames)
        .group_by("class", "bin", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.len().alias("games"), pl.col("predicted", "observed").mean())
        .sort("class", "bin")
    )

def poisson_goals(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame, cols: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expected goals per side by Poisson regression, H/D/A from the independent score grid."""
    rates = []

            SimpleImputer(strategy="median"),

def rps(y: np.ndarray, proba: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mean ranked probability score, outcomes ordered H, D, A (lower is better)."""
    order = [CLASSES.index(c) for c in ("H", "D", "A")]
    gap = np.cumsum(proba[:, order], 1) - np.cumsum(_onehot(y)[:, order], 1)
    return float(np.mean(np.sum(gap[:, :-1] ** 2, 1) / (len(CLASSES) - 1)))

def score_grid_proba(home_rate: np.ndarray, away_rate: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """P(A), P(D), P(H) for independent Poisson goals with these means, per game."""
    goals = np.arange(MAX_GOALS + 1)
    home = np.asarray(poisson.pmf(goals, home_rate[:, None]))
    away = np.asarray(poisson.pmf(goals, away_rate[:, None]))
    grid = home[:, :, None] * away[:, None, :]  # [game, home goals, away goals]
    proba = np.stack(
        [
            np.triu(grid, 1).sum((1, 2)),
            np.trace(grid, axis1=1, axis2=2),
            np.tril(grid, -1).sum((1, 2)),
        ],
        axis=1,
    )
    return proba / proba.sum(1, keepdims=True)

def fixture_features(history: pl.DataFrame, fixtures: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The fixtures with elo, games_14d_all and the player slots, built from `history`.

    `history` is match_features (played matches); `fixtures` is clean_upcoming's output.
    """
    played = to_elo_input(cast(DataFrame[CleanedMatchCols], history)).unwrap()
    elo = fixture_elo(
        played,
        fixtures.select(
            "game_id",
            season_label(pl.col("season_start")).alias("season"),
            pl.col("date").dt.date().alias("match_date"),
            "home_team",
            "away_team",
        ),
    ).select("game_id", "elo_home", "elo_away", "elo_diff")
    starters = last_starters(history)
    slots = [
        fixtures.select("game_id", pl.col(team).alias("team"))
        .join(starters, on="team", how="left")
        .drop("team")
        .rename(lambda c: c if c == "game_id" else f"{prefix}_{c}")
        for prefix, team in SIDES
    ]
    out = fixtures.select(*ID, "season_start")
    for part in [elo, games_in_window(history, fixtures), *slots]:
        out = out.join(part, on="game_id", how="left")
    return out.select(
        *ID,
        "season_start",
        "elo_home",
        "elo_away",
        "elo_diff",
        "h_games_14d_all",
        "a_games_14d_all",
        *slot_columns(),
    )

def games_in_window(history: pl.DataFrame, fixtures: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """h_ and a_games_14d_all per fixture: each team's league games in GAMES_WINDOW before it."""
    games = _team_games(history, fixtures)
    out = fixtures.select(
        "game_id", pl.col("date").dt.date().alias("day"), "home_team", "away_team"
    )
    for prefix, side in SIDES:
        counts = (
            out.join(games, left_on=side, right_on="team")
            .filter(
                (pl.col("day_right") < pl.col("day"))
                & (pl.col("day_right") >= pl.col("day") - GAMES_WINDOW)
            )
            .group_by("game_id")
            .len(name=f"{prefix}_games_14d_all")
        )
        out = out.join(counts, on="game_id", how="left")
    return out.select("game_id", pl.col("^[ha]_games_14d_all$").fill_null(0).cast(pl.Float64))

docs.title: money_printer_research.analysis.backtest
docs.text:
Backtest: would betting on the model's +EV picks against the bookmakers have paid?

Each season from settings.modeling.backtest_from is predicted walk-forward by the logistic baseline (fitted on the seasons before it, as in modeling), then priced with the 1X2 odds football-data.co.uk publishes per league and season, which collect_data downloads to settings.modeling.odds_dir (data_collection.scrape_odds).

The odds are Pinnacle's closing prices: the sharpest widely quoted market, and what a bet placed just before kick-off would get. Where they are missing the next available is used: Pinnacle's early price, the market average at closing, then Bet365's early price (ODDS_PREFERENCE; analysis.odds explains early and closing).

football-data names teams its own way ("Man United", "Paris SG"). team_names maps them to the match_features names by which team each one plays alongside on the same days, so no alias table is kept by hand.

For every game the pick is the outcome with the highest expected value of a 1-unit stake, EV = p * odds - 1. The backtest table keeps every game with its pick, EV and profit, so a strategy "bet the pick when its EV is above t" is a filter on it (summary).

A threshold picked by looking at the results flatters them, so two checks keep it honest: walk_forward_thresholds picks each season's threshold from the seasons before it only, and best_by_chance asks how often a model with no edge at all would show a best (league, threshold) cell as good as the best one here.

docs.text:
How often the best (league, threshold) cell looks this good by luck alone.

observed is the z-score of the best cell, where a cell is one league, or all of them, at one threshold. Each simulation replays the same picks at the same odds in a world where the model has no edge: every result is drawn from the bookmaker's margin-free probabilities. p_value is the share of simulations whose best cell scores at least as high as observed; far from 0, the best cell is no better than searching this many cells finds by chance.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/analysis/backtest.py 
def best_by_chance(
    table: pl.DataFrame,
    thresholds: Sequence[float] = SLIDER_THRESHOLDS,
    sims: int = 200,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """How often the best (league, threshold) cell looks this good by luck alone.

    observed is the z-score of the best cell, where a cell is one league, or all of them,
    at one threshold. Each simulation replays the same picks at the same odds in a world
    where the model has no edge: every result is drawn from the bookmaker's margin-free
    probabilities. p_value is the share of simulations whose best cell scores at least
    as high as observed; far from 0, the best cell is no better than searching this many
    cells finds by chance.
    """
    leagues = table["league"].to_numpy()
    groups = [np.ones(table.height, bool), *(leagues == lg for lg in np.unique(leagues))]
    ev = table["ev"].to_numpy()
    pick_odds = _odds_of_pick(table)

    def best_z_score(won: np.ndarray) -> float:
        return _best_z_score(np.where(won, pick_odds - 1, -1.0), ev, groups, thresholds)

    observed = best_z_score((table["pick"] == table[TARGET]).to_numpy())

    implied = 1 / table.select(f"odds_{k}" for k in OUTCOMES).to_numpy()
    market_cdf = (implied / implied.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)).cumsum(axis=1)
    pick = table["pick"].replace_strict({k: i for i, k in enumerate(OUTCOMES)}).to_numpy()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    def no_edge_best_z_score() -> float:
        # A uniform draw lands past as many cumulative probabilities as the drawn
        # outcome's index: 0 is H, 1 is D, 2 is A.
        result = (rng.random(table.height)[:, None] > market_cdf).sum(axis=1)
        return best_z_score(result == pick)

    by_chance = np.array([no_edge_best_z_score() for _ in range(sims)])
    return {"observed": observed, "p_value": float(np.mean(by_chance >= observed))}

def log_loss_vs_market(table: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Mean log loss of the model and of the bookmaker's margin-free probabilities."""
    actual = pl.col(TARGET)

    def loss(prob: dict[str, pl.Expr]) -> float:
        p = pl.coalesce(pl.when(actual == k).then(e) for k, e in prob.items())
        return float(table.select(-p.log().mean()).item())

    overround = pl.sum_horizontal(1 / pl.col(f"odds_{k}") for k in OUTCOMES)
    return {
        "model": loss({k: pl.col(f"p_{k}") for k in OUTCOMES}),
        "market": loss({k: 1 / pl.col(f"odds_{k}") / overround for k in OUTCOMES}),
    }

def picks(games: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The games (p_ and odds_ columns, and the result) with each one's pick, ev and profit.

    pick is the outcome with the highest EV; profit is what 1 unit on it returned.
    """
    p = games.select(f"p_{k}" for k in OUTCOMES).to_numpy()
    odds = games.select(f"odds_{k}" for k in OUTCOMES).to_numpy()
    ev = p * odds - 1
    best = ev.argmax(axis=1)
    rows = np.arange(len(best))
    pick = np.array(OUTCOMES)[best]
    won = pick == games[TARGET].to_numpy()
    return games.with_columns(
        pick=pl.Series(pick),
        ev=pl.Series(ev[rows, best]),
        profit=pl.Series(np.where(won, odds[rows, best] - 1, -1.0)),
    )

def team_names(odds: pl.DataFrame, games: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """league, fd_name, team: each football-data name and the games name it stands for.

    A name maps to the team it shares most game days with on the same side (home or
    away), in the same league and season. The other games of a match day add noise, but
    the right team shares every one of its days.
    """
    games = games.with_columns(day=pl.col("date").dt.date())
    pairs = pl.concat(
        odds.join(games, on=["league", "season_start", "day"]).select(
            "league", pl.col(f"fd_{side}").alias("fd_name"), pl.col(f"{side}_team").alias("team")
        )
        for side in ("home", "away")
    )
    return (
        pairs.group_by("league", "fd_name", "team")
        .len()
        .sort("len", "team", descending=[True, False])
        .group_by("league", "fd_name", maintain_order=True)
        .first()
        .drop("len")

def walk_forward(df: pl.DataFrame, seasons: list[int]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """game_id with p_H, p_D, p_A for `seasons`, each from the logistic fitted on earlier ones."""
    cols, season = columns(SELECTED), pl.col("season_start")
    frames = []
    for s in seasons:
        test = df.filter(season == s)
        proba = logistic(df.filter(season < s), test, cols)
        frames.append(
            test.select("game_id").hstack(
                pl.DataFrame({f"p_{c}": proba[:, i] for i, c in enumerate(CLASSES)})
            )
        )
    return pl.concat(frames)

def walk_forward_thresholds(
    table: pl.DataFrame, thresholds: Sequence[float] = SLIDER_THRESHOLDS
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Each season bet at a hindsight-free threshold (ThresholdSeasonCols).

    Before each season, pick the threshold that made the most on the seasons before it,
    as someone betting live would have to. The first season has nothing before it to
    choose from, so it is left out.
    """
    seasons = table["season_start"].to_numpy()
    ev = table["ev"].to_numpy()
    profit = table["profit"].to_numpy()

    rows = []
    for season in sorted(set(seasons.tolist()))[1:]:
        before = seasons < season
        chosen = max(thresholds, key=lambda t: profit[before & (ev > t)].sum())
        bets = profit[(seasons == season) & (ev > chosen)]
        roi = bets.mean() if bets.size else None
        rows.append((season, chosen, bets.size, bets.sum(), roi))
    table = pl.DataFrame(
        rows,
        schema={
            "season_start": pl.Int32,
            "min_ev": pl.Float64,
            "bets": pl.Int64,
            "profit": pl.Float64,
            "roi": pl.Float64,
        },
        orient="row",
    )
    return ThresholdSeasonCols.validate(table, lazy=True)

def unmatched_in_covered_seasons(
    cleaned_matches: pl.DataFrame, match_leagues: pl.DataFrame
) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """(unmatched, matches) up to Transfermarkt's last season, and matches after it.

    The Transfermarkt dataset stopped updating in July 2026, so the seasons after its
    last one have no Transfermarkt game at all. Their matches keep a null tm_game_id
    (features.missing marks the cells no_tm_game) and do not count as join failures.
    """
    last = match_leagues[MatchLeaguesCols.season_start].max()
    season = pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.season_start)
    covered = cleaned_matches.filter(season <= last)
    unmatched = covered[CleanedMatchCols.tm_game_id].null_count()
    return unmatched, covered.height, cleaned_matches.height - covered.height

def formation_exprs(side: Side) -> list[pl.Expr]:
    """Return the expressions that encode side.formation into side's columns."""
    raw = pl.col(side.formation).str.strip_chars()
    shape = raw.str.extract(_SHAPE)

@monad
def map_club_w_team(
    tm: DataFrame[MatchLeaguesCols], schedule: DataFrame[ScheduleCols], max_day_shift: int = 1
) -> Result[DataFrame[ClubMapCols]]:
    """_map_clubs, as an Err when there is nothing to map or a pairing is doubtful.

    Nothing to map usually means match_leagues has no league games (comp_type); a doubtful
    pairing usually means a missing ALIASES entry.
    """
    league_games = tm.filter(pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.comp_type) == "league").height
    if league_games == 0:
        return Err("map_club_w_team: match_leagues has no league games (check comp_type)")

    clubs = _map_clubs(tm, schedule, max_day_shift).if_err()
    if clubs.height == 0:
        return Err(
            f"map_club_w_team: no club matched any of {league_games:,} league games "
            "(check league names and dates between the two sources)"
        )

    doubtful = clubs.filter(
        pl.col(ClubMapCols.duplicate)
        | (
            (pl.col(ClubMapCols.coverage) < MIN_COVERAGE)
            & (pl.col(ClubMapCols.games) >= MIN_GAMES_FOR_COVERAGE)
        )
    )
    if doubtful.height:
        return Err(f"map_club_w_team: doubtful club mappings (check ALIASES):\n{doubtful}")
    return Ok(clubs)

Transfermarkt columns get a tm_ prefix so Understat's goals and date keep their names; the encoded formation columns (FormationCols) keep theirs, which only match_leagues has.

@returns(CleanedMatchCols)
def join_match_w_stat(
    tm: DataFrame[MatchLeaguesCols],
    clubs: DataFrame[ClubMapCols],
    schedule: DataFrame[ScheduleCols],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Understat schedule rows with their Transfermarkt league game (left join).

    Keyed on league, season and both teams rather than the date: a fixture is
    played once per season, and postponed or resumed games can sit days apart
    in the two sources (Udinese-Roma 2024: 14 April vs 25 April). Transfermarkt
    columns get a tm_ prefix so Understat's goals and date keep their names; the
    encoded formation columns (FormationCols) keep theirs, which only match_leagues has.
    """
    club_team = clubs.filter(~pl.col(ClubMapCols.duplicate)).select(
        ClubMapCols.club_id, ClubMapCols.team
    )
    tm_league = (
        tm.filter(pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.comp_type) == "league")
        .join(
            club_team.rename(
                {
                    ClubMapCols.club_id: MatchLeaguesCols.home_club_id,
                    ClubMapCols.team: ScheduleCols.home_team,
                }
            ),
            on=MatchLeaguesCols.home_club_id,
        )
        .join(
            club_team.rename(
                {
                    ClubMapCols.club_id: MatchLeaguesCols.away_club_id,
                    ClubMapCols.team: ScheduleCols.away_team,
                }
            ),
            on=MatchLeaguesCols.away_club_id,
        )
        .select(
            MatchLeaguesCols.league,
            MatchLeaguesCols.season_start,
            ScheduleCols.home_team,
            ScheduleCols.away_team,
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.tm_game_id).alias(CleanedMatchCols.tm_game_id),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.season).alias(CleanedMatchCols.tm_season),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.round).alias(CleanedMatchCols.tm_round),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.home_formation).alias(CleanedMatchCols.home_formation),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.away_formation).alias(CleanedMatchCols.away_formation),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.home_goals).alias(CleanedMatchCols.tm_home_goals),
            pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.away_goals).alias(CleanedMatchCols.tm_away_goals),
            pl.col(*FORMATION_COLUMNS),  # same names in L and CM, both from FormationCols
        )
    )
    # L.league / L.season_start have the same names as in S.
    keys = [
        ScheduleCols.league,
        ScheduleCols.season_start,
        ScheduleCols.home_team,
        ScheduleCols.away_team,
    ]
    return schedule.join(tm_league, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")

    matches: DataFrame[CleanedMatchCols],

    schedule: DataFrame[TeamScheduleCols],

def alias_block(schedule: pl.DataFrame) -> str:

docs.text:
Check that a pipeline step did not damage the data it passed on.

compare(before, after, key) lines up a step's input and output on a key and counts what a step should never do by accident: lose or add keys, duplicate a key, change a value it was meant to carry over, or turn a value into null. changed_rows shows the rows behind a count. Columns a step renames must be renamed in before first; columns it rewrites on purpose (canonical team names) are left out of cols.

at_morphism(f) does the same from inside a pipeline: it is f as a Kleisli arrow that logs (morphism, a, a.shape) for what f returned, after (None, a, a.shape) for the pipeline's input (a Writer, cool_stuff.writer). Logged steps compose with >> like any K, and log_report turns the log into a table:

pipeline = at_morphism(f, key="game_id") >> at_morphism(g, key="game_id")
logged = pipeline(told(df)).expect("pipeline")
log_report(logged)   # rows: None (the input), f, g; shapes, nulls, keys lost
logged.log[1].a      # the frame f returned

notebooks/data_integrity.ipynb runs these over every step of clean_data.

docs.text:
F as a logged arrow: run it, and log (f, a, a.shape) for what it returned.

On an empty log it first logs the input as (None, a, a.shape), so

(at_morphism(f) >> at_morphism(g))(told(df))

logs (None, df, df.shape), (f, f(df), ...), (g, g(f(df)), ...).

def at_morphism(
    f: Morphism[Any, Any], key: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
) -> K[Logged[Any, Missing], Logged[Any, Missing]]:
    """F as a logged arrow: run it, and log (f, a, a.shape) for what it returned.

    On an empty log it first logs the input as (None, a, a.shape), so

        (at_morphism(f) >> at_morphism(g))(told(df))

    logs (None, df, df.shape), (f, f(df), ...), (g, g(f(df)), ...).
    """
    name = name_of(f)

    def seed(x: Logged[Any, Missing]) -> Logged[Any, Missing]:
        return x if x.log else x.tell(_entry(None, x.value, key))

    logged = K(seed) >> writer(f, lambda _, b: _entry(name, b, key))
    return K(logged.run, name)

def changed_rows(
    before: pl.DataFrame,
    after: pl.DataFrame,
    key: str | Sequence[str],
    cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Long form of compare's changed and new_nulls: key, column, before, after.

    Values are shown as strings so columns of every dtype fit in one table.
    """
    key = [key] if isinstance(key, str) else list(key)
    cols = _cols(before, after, key, cols)
    after = _keys_like(before, after, key)
    both = _aligned(before, after, key, cols)
    parts = [
        both.filter(
            pl.col(c).is_not_null()
            & (pl.col(c + _AFTER).is_null() | (pl.col(c) != pl.col(c + _AFTER)))
        ).select(
            *key,
            pl.lit(c).alias("column"),
            pl.col(c).cast(pl.String).alias("before"),
            pl.col(c + _AFTER).cast(pl.String).alias("after"),
        )
        for c in cols
    ]
    text = {"column": pl.String, "before": pl.String, "after": pl.String}
    empty = pl.DataFrame(schema={**before.select(key).schema, **text})
    return pl.concat([empty, *parts]) if parts else empty

docs.title: compare(before, after, key, cols=None, step='')
docs.text:
One row: what happened to the data between before and after.

rows_before, rows_after heights lost_keys, new_keys keys on only one side dup_keys keys repeated in after (a join that fanned out) changed cells in cols that differ, null versus value excluded new_nulls cells in cols null in after but not in before

cols defaults to every column the two share; the key is left out either way. Every count but the heights should be 0 unless the step means it, such as a filter losing keys.

Source code in src/money_printer_research/clean_data/integrity.py 
def compare(
    before: pl.DataFrame,
    after: pl.DataFrame,
    key: str | Sequence[str],
    cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    step: str = "",
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row: what happened to the data between `before` and `after`.

    rows_before, rows_after  heights
    lost_keys, new_keys      keys on only one side
    dup_keys                 keys repeated in `after` (a join that fanned out)
    changed                  cells in `cols` that differ, null versus value excluded
    new_nulls                cells in `cols` null in `after` but not in `before`

    cols defaults to every column the two share; the key is left out either way. Every count but
    the heights should be 0 unless the step means it, such as a filter losing keys.
    """
    key = [key] if isinstance(key, str) else list(key)
    cols = _cols(before, after, key, cols)
    after = _keys_like(before, after, key)
    both = _aligned(before, after, key, cols)
    keys_before, keys_after = before.select(key).unique(), after.select(key).unique()

    def total(exprs: list[pl.Expr]) -> int:
        return int(both.select(pl.sum_horizontal(exprs).sum()).item()) if exprs else 0

    a, b = pl.col, lambda c: pl.col(c + _AFTER)
    changed = [(a(c).is_not_null() & b(c).is_not_null() & (a(c) != b(c))) for c in cols]
    new_nulls = [(a(c).is_not_null() & b(c).is_null()) for c in cols]
    return pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "step": [step],
            "rows_before": [before.height],
            "rows_after": [after.height],
            "lost_keys": [keys_before.join(keys_after, on=key, how="anti").height],
            "new_keys": [keys_after.join(keys_before, on=key, how="anti").height],
            "dup_keys": [after.height - keys_after.height],
            "changed": [total(changed)],
            "new_nulls": [total(new_nulls)],
        }
    )

def log_report(logged: Logged[Any, Missing]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The log as a table, one row per entry in order: the input first, then each morphism.

    more_nulls lists the columns with more nulls than in the entry before, a column
    the morphism added counting from 0; with a key, lost_keys to new_nulls are compare's
    counts against the entry before. The first row has none of these.
    """
    entries = list(logged.log)
    rows = [_row(prev, cur) for prev, cur in zip([None, *entries], entries, strict=False)]
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, infer_schema_length=None)

def apply_lifted(f: Callable[[Any], Any], x: Any) -> Result[Any]:

    """Ok of every value if all are Ok, else every Err summed into one (errors accumulate).

    a failure in one does not hide a failure in another. Typed for up to 6.

A Kleisli arrow A -> Result[B]: callable, and a monoid under >>.

f >> g is Kleisli composition (f >=> g): run f, feed its Ok into g, stop at the first Err. It is associative, and IDENTITY (pure) is its unit:

def compose(*morphisms: Morphism[Any, Result[Any]]) -> K[Any, Any]:
    """Fold the arrows with >> from IDENTITY (mconcat): f1 >=> f2 >=> ...

    Typed for up to 8 steps: compose(lift(f), lift(g)) is K[A, C] when f: A -> B
    and g: B -> C, and a step whose input does not match the previous output is a
    type error. The result is a K, so compose(...) >> compose(...) works; for more
    than 8 steps, join groups that way or nest compose.
    """
    if not morphisms:
        return IDENTITY
    first, *rest = morphisms
    start = first if isinstance(first, K) else K(first, name_of(first))
    return reduce(K.__rshift__, rest, start)  # IDENTITY >> f == f, so skip it

def returns[M: pa.DataFrameModel, **P](
    model: type[M],
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, pl.DataFrame]], Callable[P, Result[DataFrame[M]]]]:
    """Check f's returned frame against `model`, giving Result[DataFrame[M]].

    Like a Rust fn returning Result<DataFrame<M>, Err>: an exception or a schema
    failure becomes Err naming f.
    """

    def decorate(f: Callable[P, pl.DataFrame]) -> Callable[P, Result[DataFrame[M]]]:
        validate = check(model)
        label = name_of(f)

        @wraps(f)
        def run(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Result[DataFrame[M]]:
            try:
                df = f(*args, **kwargs)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every failure becomes an Err
                return Err(f"{label}: {e!r}", cause=e)
            return validate(df).map_err(lambda reason: f"{label} -> {reason}")

        return run

    return decorate

def writer[A, B, W](
    f: Morphism[A, Any], note: Callable[[A, B], W]
) -> K[Logged[A, W], Logged[B, W]]:
    """Lift f into the logged category: f on the value, then note(input, output) on the log.

    f may return a plain value or a Result (auto lift, as with K); an exception or
    an Err from f is the arrow's Err. note runs only on success.
    """

    def run(x: Logged[A, W]) -> Result[Logged[B, W]]:
        return apply_lifted(f, x.value).map(lambda b: Logged(b, x.log + (note(x.value, b),)))

    return K(run, name_of(f))

def export(db_file: Path, out_dir: Path, league_ids: list[str], first_season: int) -> None:
    """Write the filtered tables to parquet and print their row counts.

    league_ids: Transfermarkt competition ids of the leagues to keep, e.g. ["GB1", "ES1"].
    first_season: first season start year; appearances keep one extra season so
                  rolling windows at the start of `first_season` have history.

        raise ValueError("league_ids is empty: set transfermarkt.leagues in the config")
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    leagues = ", ".join(f"'{c}'" for c in league_ids)
    in_scope = f"games.competition_id IN ({leagues}) AND {SEASON_YEAR} >= {first_season}"

    con = duckdb.connect(str(db_file), read_only=True)
    try:
        _create_scope_tables(con, in_scope)
        for name, sql in _export_queries(first_season).items():
            path = _copy_checked(con, name, sql, out_dir)
            row = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM '{path}'").fetchone()
            print(f"saved {name:13s} {row[0] if row else 0:>9,} rows", flush=True)
    finally:
        con.close()

def save_checked(df: pd.DataFrame, out: Path, schema: RawSchema) -> None:
    """Write `df` to `out` (.parquet or .csv) only if it matches every column of `schema`.

    The file is written next to `out` first and checked from disk, so a frame
    that fails the check never leaves a file that later runs would skip.
    """
    tmp = out.with_name(f"{out.stem}.part{out.suffix}")
    if out.suffix == ".parquet":
        df.to_parquet(tmp)
    else:
        df.to_csv(tmp, index=False)
    try:
        check_collected(tmp, schema)
    except ValueError:
        tmp.unlink()
        raise
    tmp.replace(out)

Double Poisson match model driven by pre-match Elo, with optional Dixon-Coles.

Home and away goals are modelled as two Poisson variables whose log-rates are linear in the pre-match Elo difference. Outcome probabilities (H/D/A) come from the joint score grid. Everything is walk-forward: each season is predicted by a model fitted only on earlier seasons, and Elo ratings are always pre-match.

Log loss, ranked probability score and accuracy of p_home/p_draw/p_away.

def evaluate(pred: DataFrame[PredictionCols]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Log loss, ranked probability score and accuracy of p_home/p_draw/p_away."""
    p = pred.select(PredictionCols.p_home, PredictionCols.p_draw, PredictionCols.p_away).to_numpy()
    y = np.array([OUTCOMES.index(r) for r in pred[RESULT].to_list()])
    onehot = np.eye(len(OUTCOMES))[y]
    log_loss = float(-np.log(np.clip(p[np.arange(len(y)), y], EPS, None)).mean())
    # RPS: squared gaps of the cumulative distributions; the last one is always 0.
    rps = float((((np.cumsum(p, 1) - np.cumsum(onehot, 1))[:, :-1]) ** 2).sum(1).mean() / 2)
    acc = float((p.argmax(1) == y).mean())
    return {"log_loss": log_loss, "rps": rps, "accuracy": acc, "n": len(y)}

Pre-match elo_home, elo_away and elo_diff for unplayed fixtures.

fixtures has EloInputCols' season, match_date, home_team and away_team. The ratings are those after every played match; a fixture has no result, so it moves none. A fixture in a season the played matches have not reached starts that season first (promoted teams, regression toward base), as get_elo would.

def fixture_elo(
    played: DataFrame[EloInputCols], fixtures: pl.DataFrame, params: EloParams = DEFAULT_ELO
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Pre-match elo_home, elo_away and elo_diff for unplayed fixtures.

    `fixtures` has EloInputCols' season, match_date, home_team and away_team. The ratings
    are those after every played match; a fixture has no result, so it moves none. A
    fixture in a season the played matches have not reached starts that season first
    (promoted teams, regression toward base), as get_elo would.
    """
    played = DataFrame[EloInputCols](played.sort(EloCols.match_date))
    *_, rating, last_season_teams, current_season = _replay(played, params)
    cols = [EloCols.season, EloCols.home_team, EloCols.away_team]
    teams_by_season = _teams_by_season(pl.concat([played.select(cols), fixtures.select(cols)]))  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
    fixtures = fixtures.sort(EloCols.match_date)
    elo_home: list[float] = []
    elo_away: list[float] = []
    for season, home, away in fixtures.select(cols).iter_rows():
        if season != current_season:
            this_season_teams = teams_by_season[season]
            _start_season(rating, last_season_teams, this_season_teams, params)
            last_season_teams, current_season = this_season_teams, season
        elo_home.append(rating[home])
        elo_away.append(rating[away])
    return _with_diff(fixtures, elo_home, elo_away)

def get_elo(
    matches: DataFrame[EloInputCols], params: EloParams = DEFAULT_ELO
) -> DataFrame[EloCols]:
    """Add pre-match elo_home, elo_away and elo_diff (home minus away, no home bonus).

    Promoted teams start each season at the mean end-of-season rating of the
    teams that went down, which keeps the league average stable.
    """
    df = DataFrame[EloInputCols](matches.sort(EloCols.match_date))
    elo_home, elo_away, *_ = _replay(df, params)
    return EloCols.validate(_with_diff(df, elo_home, elo_away), lazy=True)

def outcome_probs(grid: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
    """(n, 3) probabilities in OUTCOMES order: home win, draw, away win."""
    shape = grid.shape[1:]
    home = np.tril(np.ones(shape), k=-1)  # h > a
    draw = np.eye(shape[0])
    away = np.triu(np.ones(shape), k=1)  # a > h
    return np.stack([(grid * m).sum(axis=(1, 2)) for m in (home, draw, away)], axis=1)

docs.text:
Joint probability of each scoreline; grid[i, h, a] = P(home=h, away=a).

def score_grid(
    lam: FloatArray, mu: FloatArray, rho: float = 0.0, max_goals: int = MAX_GOALS
) -> FloatArray:
    """Joint probability of each scoreline; grid[i, h, a] = P(home=h, away=a)."""
    goals = np.arange(max_goals + 1)
    # scipy's stubs type pmf as float; with array inputs it returns an (n, g) array.
    ph = _as_float(poisson.pmf(goals[None, :], lam[:, None]))
    pa = _as_float(poisson.pmf(goals[None, :], mu[:, None]))
    grid = ph[:, :, None] * pa[:, None, :]
    if rho:
        grid = grid * _dc_tau(lam, mu, rho, max_goals)
    return grid / grid.sum(axis=(1, 2), keepdims=True)

@returns(EloInputCols)
def to_elo_input(matches: DataFrame[CleanedMatchCols]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """cleaned_matches -> EloInputCols: season label, date only, full-time goals and result."""
    ei = EloInputCols
    start = pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.season_start)
    hg, ag = pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.home_goals), pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.away_goals)
    return matches.select(
        season_label(start).alias(ei.season),
        pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.date).dt.date().alias(ei.match_date),
        pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.home_team).alias(ei.home_team),
        pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.away_team).alias(ei.away_team),
        hg.alias(ei.full_time_home_goals),
        ag.alias(ei.full_time_away_goals),
        pl.when(hg > ag)
        .then(pl.lit("H"))
        .when(hg == ag)
        .then(pl.lit("D"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("A"))
        .alias(ei.full_time_result),
    )

def walk_forward(
    df: DataFrame[EloCols], test_seasons: list[str], dixon_coles: bool = True
) -> DataFrame[PredictionCols]:
    """Predict each test season with a model fitted on all earlier seasons."""
    seasons = sorted(df[EloCols.season].unique().to_list())
    predictions: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
    for season in test_seasons:
        earlier = [s for s in seasons if s < season]
        train = df.filter(pl.col(EloCols.season).is_in(earlier))
        test = df.filter(pl.col(EloCols.season) == season)
        predictions.append(_predict_season(train, test, dixon_coles))
    return PredictionCols.validate(pl.concat(predictions), lazy=True)

def player_fatigue(player_matches: DataFrame[FatigueInputCols]) -> DataFrame[PlayerFatigueCols]:
    """player_matches plus pre-match fatigue columns (see FATIGUE_COLS)."""
    minutes = pl.col(FatigueInputCols.minutes)
    played = minutes.is_not_null().cast(pl.Int64)
    pm = (
        player_matches.join(
            _team_game_index(player_matches),
            on=[FatigueInputCols.team_id, FatigueInputCols.game_id],
            validate="m:1",
        )
        .sort(FatigueInputCols.player_id, FatigueInputCols.match_date)
        .with_columns(
            pl.col(FatigueInputCols.match_date)
            .diff()
            .dt.total_days()
            .over(FatigueInputCols.player_id)
            .alias(PlayerFatigueCols.rest_days),
            _prev_window(minutes, "7d").alias(PlayerFatigueCols.min_7d),
            _prev_window(played, "7d").alias(PlayerFatigueCols.n_7d),
            _prev_window(minutes, "28d").alias(PlayerFatigueCols.min_28d),
            # A new streak starts when the player missed the team's previous game,
            # or at his first game for a team (a transfer starts a new run).
            (pl.col(TEAM_GAME_NO).diff().over(_STREAK_KEYS) != 1)
            .fill_null(True)
            .alias(NEW_STREAK),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col(NEW_STREAK).cast(pl.Int32).cum_sum().over(_STREAK_KEYS).alias(STREAK_ID)
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.int_range(pl.len())
            .over(*_STREAK_KEYS, STREAK_ID)
            .alias(PlayerFatigueCols.streak_prev)
        )
    )
    out = pm.with_columns(_fatigue_score().round(1).alias(PlayerFatigueCols.fatigue_score)).drop(
        TEAM_GAME_NO, NEW_STREAK, STREAK_ID
    )
    return PlayerFatigueCols.validate(out, lazy=True)

player_stat has no date or side, so both come from the match: match_date is the date part of the kick-off, and a player is home when his team is the home_team. Duplicate (game_id, player_id) rows, which Understat repeats for a few games, are dropped.

def player_matches(
    player_stat: DataFrame[PlayerStatCols], matches: DataFrame[CleanedMatchCols]
) -> DataFrame[FatigueInputCols]:
    """player_stat with each match's date and the player's side, one row per player per match.

    player_stat has no date or side, so both come from the match: match_date is the
    date part of the kick-off, and a player is home when his team is the home_team.
    Duplicate (game_id, player_id) rows, which Understat repeats for a few games, are dropped.
    """
    match_info: DataFrame[MatchSideCols] = MatchSideCols.validate(
        matches.select(
            pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.game_id).alias(MatchSideCols.game_id),
            pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.date).dt.date().alias(MatchSideCols.match_date),
            pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.home_team).alias(MatchSideCols.home_team),
        )
    )
    return FatigueInputCols.validate(
        player_stat.unique(
            [PlayerStatCols.game_id, PlayerStatCols.player_id], keep="first", maintain_order=True
        )
        .join(match_info, on=PlayerStatCols.game_id, how="inner", validate="m:1")
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col(PlayerStatCols.team) == pl.col(MatchSideCols.home_team)).alias(
                FatigueInputCols.is_home
            )
        )
        .drop(MatchSideCols.home_team)
    )

def team_fatigue(fatigue: DataFrame[PlayerFatigueCols]) -> DataFrame[TeamFatigueCols]:
    """Mean starter fatigue per side, one row per game_id.

    A side with no starters recorded gets null in all of its columns, not 0.
    """
    starters = fatigue.filter(pl.col(PlayerFatigueCols.position) != "Sub")
    home, away = pl.col(PlayerFatigueCols.is_home), ~pl.col(PlayerFatigueCols.is_home)
    score, min_7d = pl.col(PlayerFatigueCols.fatigue_score), pl.col(PlayerFatigueCols.min_7d)
    out = (
        starters.group_by(PlayerFatigueCols.game_id)
        .agg(
            score.filter(home).mean().alias(TeamFatigueCols.h_fatigue),
            score.filter(away).mean().alias(TeamFatigueCols.a_fatigue),
            pl.when(home.any()).then(min_7d.filter(home).sum()).alias(TeamFatigueCols.h_min_7d),
            pl.when(away.any()).then(min_7d.filter(away).sum()).alias(TeamFatigueCols.a_min_7d),
        )
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col(TeamFatigueCols.h_fatigue) - pl.col(TeamFatigueCols.a_fatigue)).alias(
                TeamFatigueCols.fatigue_diff
            )
        )
    )
    return TeamFatigueCols.validate(out, lazy=True)

docs.title: money_printer_research.features.calendar
docs.text:
Plan A: every club's full match calendar (league, cups, Europe) from Transfermarkt.

Understat only has league games, so a team that played in Europe on Wednesday looks rested for Saturday. Transfermarkt games (match_leagues) have all competitions. club_calendar computes pre-match schedule features on that full calendar, and team_schedule_features attaches them to each Understat game as h_ / a_ columns, through the tm_game_id that join_match_w_stat put on cleaned_matches.

All features use only games before the match, except the look-ahead ones (days_to_next_all, next_is_europe), which use fixtures already scheduled.

docs.title: MAX_GAP_DAYS = 30 module-attribute
docs.text: Cap on rest_days_all and days_to_next_all: beyond a month every club is fully rested, and the raw gaps reach years for clubs that spent seasons outside the five leagues. A club's first game in the data, with no previous one, gets MAX_GAP_DAYS of rest.

def club_calendar(tm: DataFrame[MatchLeaguesCols]) -> DataFrame[ClubCalendarCols]:
    """One row per club per game with the schedule features, computed on all competitions."""
    sides = [(MatchLeaguesCols.home_club_id, True), (MatchLeaguesCols.away_club_id, False)]
    cal = pl.concat(
        [
            tm.select(
                pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.tm_game_id).alias(ClubCalendarCols.tm_game_id),
                pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.date).alias(ClubCalendarCols.date),
                pl.col(MatchLeaguesCols.comp_type).alias(ClubCalendarCols.comp_type),
                pl.col(own).alias(ClubCalendarCols.club_id),
                pl.lit(is_home).alias(ClubCalendarCols.is_home),
            )
            for own, is_home in sides
        ]
    ).sort(ClubCalendarCols.club_id, ClubCalendarCols.date, ClubCalendarCols.tm_game_id)

    comp, date = pl.col(ClubCalendarCols.comp_type), pl.col(ClubCalendarCols.date)
    any_game = date.is_not_null()
    europe_away = (comp == "europe") & ~pl.col(ClubCalendarCols.is_home)
    out = cal.with_columns(
        date.diff()
        .dt.total_days()
        .over(ClubCalendarCols.club_id)
        .clip(0, MAX_GAP_DAYS)
        .fill_null(MAX_GAP_DAYS)  # first game in the data: no previous one, fully rested
        .alias(ClubCalendarCols.rest_days_all),
        _prior_count(7, any_game).alias(ClubCalendarCols.games_7d_all),
        _prior_count(14, any_game).alias(ClubCalendarCols.games_14d_all),
        _prior_count(14, comp != "league").alias(ClubCalendarCols.non_league_14d),
        europe_away.shift(1)
        .over(ClubCalendarCols.club_id)
        .fill_null(False)
        .alias(ClubCalendarCols.prev_europe_away),
        (date.shift(-1).over(ClubCalendarCols.club_id) - date)
        .dt.total_days()
        .clip(0, MAX_GAP_DAYS)
        .alias(ClubCalendarCols.days_to_next_all),
        (comp.shift(-1).over(ClubCalendarCols.club_id) == "europe")
        .fill_null(False)
        .alias(ClubCalendarCols.next_is_europe),
    )
    return ClubCalendarCols.validate(out, lazy=True)

@returns(TeamScheduleCols)
def team_schedule_features(
    tm: DataFrame[MatchLeaguesCols], cleaned_matches: DataFrame[CleanedMatchCols]
) -> DataFrame[TeamScheduleCols]:
    """Per Understat game_id: h_* and a_* schedule features from the full calendar."""
    game_map = cleaned_matches.select(
        CleanedMatchCols.game_id, CleanedMatchCols.tm_game_id
    ).drop_nulls()
    cal = club_calendar(tm).join(
        game_map, on=ClubCalendarCols.tm_game_id, how="inner", validate="m:1"
    )

    def side(is_home: bool, prefix: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
        return cal.filter(pl.col(ClubCalendarCols.is_home) == is_home).select(
            CleanedMatchCols.game_id, *(pl.col(c).alias(f"{prefix}{c}") for c in SCHEDULE_FEATURES)
        )

    out = side(True, "h_").join(
        side(False, "a_"), on=CleanedMatchCols.game_id, how="full", coalesce=True, validate="1:1"
    )
    return TeamScheduleCols.validate(out, lazy=True)

def player_form(fatigue: DataFrame[PlayerFatigueCols]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add prev_xg, prev_xa, prev_min and the per-90 rates xg90, xa90 and form90.

    form90 is (prev_xg + prev_xa) per 90: the player's expected goal involvement.
    """
    per90 = pl.when(pl.col("prev_min") >= MIN_PREV_MIN).then(90 / pl.col("prev_min"))
    return (
        fatigue.sort(
            FatigueInputCols.player_id, FatigueInputCols.match_date, FatigueInputCols.game_id
        )
        .with_columns(
            _prev(FatigueInputCols.xg).alias("prev_xg"),
            _prev(FatigueInputCols.xa).alias("prev_xa"),
            _prev(FatigueInputCols.minutes).alias("prev_min"),
        )
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col("prev_xg") * per90).alias("xg90"),
            (pl.col("prev_xa") * per90).alias("xa90"),
            ((pl.col("prev_xg") + pl.col("prev_xa")) * per90).alias("form90"),
        )
    )

def player_slots(form: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per game_id: each side's starters, ordered GK first, as slot columns."""
    starters = (
        form.filter(pl.col(FatigueInputCols.position) != "Sub")
        .with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col(FatigueInputCols.is_home))
            .then(pl.lit("h"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit("a"))
            .alias("side"),
            pl.col(FatigueInputCols.position)
            .replace_strict({p: i for i, p in enumerate(POSITION_ORDER)})
            .alias("_order"),
        )
        .sort(FatigueInputCols.game_id, "side", "_order", FatigueInputCols.player_id)
        .with_columns(
            (pl.int_range(pl.len()).over(FatigueInputCols.game_id, "side") + 1).alias("slot")
        )
        .filter(pl.col("slot") <= N_SLOTS)
    )
    long = starters.unpivot(
        index=[FatigueInputCols.game_id, "side", "slot"],
        on=list(PLAYER_SLOT_FEATURES),
        variable_name="feature",
    ).with_columns(
        pl.format("{}_player{}_{}", "side", "slot", "feature").alias("column"),
        pl.col("value").cast(pl.Float64),
    )
    wide = long.pivot(on="column", index=FatigueInputCols.game_id, values="value")

match_features keeps its nulls and gains no columns. missing_table lists every null cell (game_id, column) with the side it belongs to and the reason it is null:

@returns(MissingCols)
def missing_table(match_features: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per null cell of match_features: game_id, column, side and reason (MissingCols)."""
    key = CleanedMatchCols.game_id
    cells = (
        match_features.select(
            key, *(pl.col(c).is_null().alias(c) for c in match_features.columns if c != key)
        )
        .unpivot(index=key, variable_name="column", value_name="is_null")
        .filter(pl.col("is_null"))
        .drop("is_null")
    )
    sources = match_features.select(
        key,
        *(pl.col(f"{s}_{LINEUP_PROBE}").is_null().alias(f"{s}_no_lineup") for s in SIDES),
        *(pl.col(f"{s}_{SCHEDULE_PROBE}").is_null().alias(f"{s}_no_schedule") for s in SIDES),
        pl.col(CleanedMatchCols.tm_game_id).is_null().alias("no_tm_game"),
        *(
            pl.col(f"{p}_formation").is_null().alias(f"{s}_no_formation")
            for s, p in (("h", "home"), ("a", "away"))
        ),
    )
    column = pl.col("column")
    side = pl.col("side")
    per_side = {
        name: pl.when(side == "h").then(pl.col(f"h_{name}")).otherwise(pl.col(f"a_{name}"))
        for name in ("no_lineup", "no_schedule", "no_formation")
    }
    is_slot = pl.col("slot").is_not_null()
    empty_slot = (pl.col("feature") == EMPTY_SLOT_PROBE).any().over(key, "side", "slot") & is_slot
    either_no_lineup = pl.col("h_no_lineup") | pl.col("a_no_lineup")
    reason = (
        pl.when(is_slot & per_side["no_lineup"])
        .then(pl.lit("no_lineup"))
        .when(empty_slot)
        .then(pl.lit("short_lineup"))
        .when(is_slot & pl.col("feature").is_in(PER90))
        .then(pl.lit("too_few_minutes"))
        .when(column.is_in(FATIGUE_COLUMNS) & side.is_not_null() & per_side["no_lineup"])
        .then(pl.lit("no_lineup"))
        .when((column == "fatigue_diff") & either_no_lineup)
        .then(pl.lit("no_lineup"))
        .when(column.is_in(SCHEDULE_COLUMNS) & per_side["no_schedule"])
        .then(pl.lit("no_schedule"))
        .when(column.is_in(SCHEDULE_COLUMNS) & column.str.ends_with("_days_to_next_all"))
        .then(pl.lit("no_next_game"))
        .when(column.is_in(TM_COLUMNS) & pl.col("no_tm_game"))
        .then(pl.lit("no_tm_game"))
        .when(column.is_in(FORMATION_COLUMNS) & side.is_not_null() & per_side["no_formation"])
        .then(pl.lit("no_formation"))
        .when(column.str.ends_with("_variant") & column.is_in(FORMATION_COLUMNS))
        .then(pl.lit("plain_shape"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("other"))
    )
    return (
        cells.join(sources, on=key, how="left")
        .with_columns(
            pl.coalesce(
                pl.when(pl.any_horizontal(column.str.starts_with(p) for p in prefixes)).then(
                    pl.lit(s)
                )
                for s, prefixes in _SIDE_PREFIX.items()
            ).alias("side"),
            column.str.extract(_SLOT, 1).alias("slot"),
            column.str.extract(_SLOT, 2).alias("feature"),
        )
        .with_columns(reason.alias("reason"))
        .select(key, "column", "side", "reason")
        .sort(key, maintain_order=True)
    )

share is the nulls over every cell of the group: rows times its number of columns.

def null_report(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Nulls per feature group (see feature_group), most first; groups without nulls left out.

    share is the nulls over every cell of the group: rows times its number of columns.
    """
    counts = df.null_count().row(0, named=True)
    return (
        pl.DataFrame(
            {"group": [feature_group(c) for c in counts], "nulls": list(counts.values())},
            schema={"group": pl.String, "nulls": pl.Int64},
        )
        .group_by("group", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.len().alias("columns"), pl.col("nulls").sum())
        .filter(pl.col("nulls") > 0)
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col("nulls") / (pl.col("columns") * max(df.height, 1))).round(4).alias("share")
        )
        .sort("nulls", descending=True, maintain_order=True)
    )

def check_clean() -> None:
    """Entry point `check_clean`: validate every clean CSV; exit 1 if any fails."""
    out = settings.clean.out_dir
    failed = 0
    for name in CLEAN_FILES:
        path = out / f"{name}.csv"

            print(f"MISSING {path}", flush=True)

        try:
