docs.title: Data pipeline
docs.text:
The pipeline runs in three steps. Each step reads only what the previous one wrote, and every frame is checked against a schema on the way, so a source that changes shape fails at the step where it changed.

collect_data   Understat schedule and player stats, odds, Transfermarkt tables
     │           -> raw CSV and Parquet files
clean_data     clean            -> match_leagues, clubs, cleaned_matches, player_stat
     │         extract_features -> elo, fatigue, schedule, players, match_features
check_clean    validate every CSV in the clean output folder
Step Command Reads Writes 1. Collect collect_data Understat, football-data.co.uk, Transfermarkt Raw CSV and Parquet files 2. Clean clean_data Raw files match_leagues, clubs, cleaned_matches, player_stat 3. Features clean_data Clean frames (in memory) elo, fatigue, schedule, players, match_features

clean_data runs steps 2 and 3 together and writes all nine CSVs to the clean output folder (data/clean by default). check_clean validates them afterwards.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Understat, through soccerdata: the league schedule with goals and xG, and every player's stats for every league match. Understat covers league games only.
  • Transfermarkt, from dcaribou/transfermarkt-datasets: every club's full calendar (leagues, domestic cups, European and other games), the formations each side started with, and the list of competitions.

Understat gives the target and the per-player stats; Transfermarkt fills in the games Understat does not see, which matter for rest and congestion. The two are joined through a learned club-to-team map (see Clean).

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Cleaning and feature steps return a Result (Ok or Err) from the cool_stuff package instead of raising. Independent steps run together with all_ok, which collects every failure into one Err; dependent steps stop at the first Err. clean_data turns a final Err into an exception that names the failing step.

docs.title: 2. Clean
docs.text:
clean in money_printer_research.clean_data turns the collected files into four clean tables. uv run clean_data runs it, writes each table as <name>.csv to the clean output folder, then runs feature extraction.

Output Schema One row per match_leagues.csv MatchLeaguesCols Transfermarkt game, any competition clubs.csv ClubMapCols Transfermarkt club cleaned_matches.csv CleanedMatchCols Understat league match player_stat.csv PlayerStatCols Player per Understat match

The steps below run in this order. Each one checks its input and output against a schema.

docs.title: Read
docs.text: clean_data.read loads the raw files and validates them against their raw schemas: the Understat schedule CSV, every player-stat Parquet file under the Understat output folder, and Transfermarkt games.parquet and competitions.parquet.

docs.title: Clean the Understat schedule
docs.text:
clean_match_stat (in clean_data.match_stat):

  1. Keeps played matches only (is_result is true).
  2. Adds season_start, the first year of the season: 1415 becomes 2014.
  3. Checks every team name against the alias table, then replaces it with the club's canonical name (see Team names).
  4. Validates the result as ScheduleCols.

docs.title: Clean the Understat player stats
docs.text: clean_player_stat (in clean_data.player_stat) adds season_start, checks and normalises team names the same way, and validates the result as PlayerStatCols.

docs.title: Encode formations
docs.text: encode_formation (in clean_data.formation) turns each Transfermarkt formation string, such as "4-2-3-1" or "4-4-2 double 6", into numbers for both sides: the shape, the variant, the number of defenders, midfielders and forwards, and the number of lines. A formation that does not parse gets null in every encoded column. unknown_formations lists those for review.

docs.title: Join games to competitions
docs.text:
join_match_w_league (in clean_data.match_leagues) joins the Transfermarkt games to their competitions and adds:

  • comp_type: league, domestic_cup, europe or other. European ties are recognised by competition id, because Transfermarkt files some of them under type other; the EFL Cup is added by hand because the competitions table does not list it.
  • league: the Understat league name for the five leagues, null otherwise.

The result is match_leagues.csv.

docs.title: Map clubs to teams
docs.text:
Transfermarkt identifies clubs by id and Understat by name, and the two spell clubs differently. map_club_w_team (in clean_data.map_club_team) learns the map from the fixtures themselves rather than from names: a Transfermarkt league game and an Understat game are the same fixture when the league and score match and the dates are at most one day apart. Each club id is paired with the Understat team it matches most often.

The step fails, with the doubtful rows in the error, when:

  • two club ids pair with the same team, or
  • a club with at least 10 league games has fewer than 90% of them backing its pairing.

Either usually means a missing alias. The result is clubs.csv.

docs.title: Join Understat matches to Transfermarkt games
docs.text:
join_match_w_stat (in clean_data.match) left-joins each Understat match to its Transfermarkt league game on league, season, home team and away team, using the club map. It does not join on the date: postponed or resumed games can sit days apart in the two sources. Transfermarkt columns get a tm_ prefix; the encoded formation columns keep their names.

Every Understat match keeps its row. The step fails if more than 1% of matches find no Transfermarkt game. The result is cleaned_matches.csv.

docs.title: Team names
docs.text:
clean_data.rename_team_names gives every club one canonical lowercase name shared by both sources. A raw name is lowercased, stripped of dots and trimmed, then looked up in ALIASES (in clean_data.aliases_team).

ALIASES is also an allowlist: a name that is not in it fails the step instead of silently splitting one club in two. When a new season brings new names, print paste-ready lines and add them to the table:

from money_printer_research.clean_data.rename_team_names import alias_block

print(alias_block(schedule))

docs.title: Checking a step did no damage
docs.text:
clean_data.integrity compares a step's input with its output on a key and counts keys lost, added or duplicated, values changed, and values turned into null. at_morphism(f, key=...) does the same from inside a pipeline: it is f as a Kleisli arrow that logs (morphism, a, a.shape) for what f returned, after (None, a, a.shape) for the pipeline's input (a Writer over Result, in cool_stuff.writer). Each entry keeps its frame, and the entry before it is the morphism's input. Logged arrows compose with >> like any K, and trace(*steps, key=...) logs a whole chain:

from money_printer_research.clean_data.integrity import log_report, trace
from money_printer_research.clean_data.match_stat import MATCH_STAT_STEPS
from money_printer_research.cool_stuff import told

logged = trace(*MATCH_STAT_STEPS, key="game_id")(told(raw_schedule)).expect("schedule")
log_report(logged)  # rows: None (the input), then each morphism; shape, nulls, keys lost
logged.log[1].a  # the frame the first morphism returned

notebooks/data_integrity.ipynb runs it over every step, from the raw files to match_features.csv and on to the CSVs on disk, and checks that Understat and Transfermarkt agree on the score of every matched game.

docs.title: 1. Collect
docs.text:
uv run collect_data downloads every source the clean step reads. It runs four collectors from money_printer_research.data_collection, fastest first.

Every collector follows the same two rules:

  • Resumable. A file that already exists is skipped, so the command can be stopped and started again.
  • Checked before saving. A frame is written to <name>.part.<ext>, read back and validated against its full raw schema (schema.check_collected), and only then renamed to its final name. A source that changed shape fails at download time and leaves no file behind, so the next run tries again.

docs.title: Understat schedule
docs.text:
collect_schedule reads the schedule of every configured league and season in one soccerdata call and writes a single CSV (data/raw/xg_schedule.csv with the shipped settings).

  • One row per fixture, played or not, with goals, xG and the Understat game_id.
  • Checked against UnderstatScheduleRaw.
  • Skipped when the file already holds every configured season.

docs.title: football-data.co.uk odds
docs.text:
collect_odds downloads the 1X2 bookmaker odds backtest bets against, one CSV per league and season: <odds_dir>/<league>/<season>.csv, for example data/raw/odds/ENG-Premier League/2024-25.csv.

  • One small request per league and season.
  • Every season is downloaded once, except the last configured one, which is fetched again on each run because it grows as it is played.
  • A season football-data has not published yet is printed as not published yet and skipped.
  • No raw schema yet; the download goes to <file>.part and is renamed when complete.

docs.title: Understat player stats
docs.text:
collect_player_stats writes one Parquet file per league and season: <out_dir>/<league>/<season>.parquet, for example data/raw/player_stats/ENG-Premier League/2014-15.parquet.

  • One row per player per match: minutes, position, goals, xG, xA and more.
  • Checked against UnderstatPlayerRaw.
  • Understat serves one page per match, so this is the slow step. soccerdata caches pages under the Understat cache folder.
  • When one match has no rosters, the whole season read fails; the collector then falls back to reading match by match and prints the matches it skipped.
  • A league and season that fails is printed as FAILED and skipped; the next run retries it.

docs.title: Transfermarkt
docs.text:
collect_transfermarkt downloads the dcaribou/transfermarkt-datasets DuckDB file once, then exports three tables to Parquet in the Transfermarkt output folder:

File Rows kept Raw schema competitions.parquet Every competition TransfermarktCompetitionsRaw games.parquet Every game, in any competition, involving a club that played in the configured leagues, from the first season on TransfermarktGamesRaw appearances.parquet Every appearance by a player who played in those leagues, from one season earlier none yet

Appearances keep one extra season so rolling windows at the start of the first season have history.

  • The download streams to <file>.part and is renamed when complete, so a broken download never looks finished.
  • The dataset stopped updating in July 2026, so both the download and the export are skipped once their files exist. Delete them to force a refresh.

docs.title: 3. Features
docs.text:
extract_features in money_printer_research.clean_data builds the pre-match features from the clean tables and joins them onto the matches. uv run clean_data runs it after clean and writes six more CSVs.

Every feature uses only what was known at kick-off: rolling windows exclude the current match, and Elo ratings are taken before the match is played. The two exceptions are noted under Schedule.

Output Schema Built by elo.csv EloCols features.get_elo fatigue.csv TeamFatigueCols features.get_fatigue schedule.csv TeamScheduleCols features.team_schedule_features players.csv PLAYER_SLOTS features.get_player_features match_features.csv MatchFeaturesCols clean_data.join.join_features missing.csv MissingCols features.missing.missing_table model_frame.csv model_frame_schema features.impute.model_frame

The first four are computed independently, so if several fail, every error comes back together.

docs.title: Elo
docs.text:
get_elo replays every league match in date order and records each side's rating before kick-off as elo_home and elo_away, with elo_diff = elo_home - elo_away.

  • Update size k = 15, home advantage of 40 points in the expectation, base rating 1500. These were tuned by walk-forward log loss; the surface is flat.
  • The update is scaled by goal difference: 1 for one goal, 1.5 for two, then (11 + gd) / 8.
  • Promoted teams start each season at the mean end-of-season rating of the teams that went down, which keeps the league average stable.
  • Every team starts level in 2014/15, so treat that season as warm-up.

features.elo also holds a double Poisson match model driven by elo_diff (walk_forward, evaluate), with an optional Dixon-Coles correction. It predicts each season with a model fitted only on earlier seasons.

docs.title: Fatigue
docs.text:
get_fatigue works per player, then summarises each side's starters.

For every player and match, player_fatigue computes the load before kick-off: rest days, matches and minutes in the last 7 days, minutes in the last 28 days, and consecutive team games played. These combine into a fatigue_score from 0 to 100, with hand-set weights:

Weight Term (each scaled to 0 to 1) 0.35 Minutes in the last 7 days (180 is full) 0.25 Short rest 0.20 Consecutive games played 0.20 Acute to chronic workload ratio above 1

team_fatigue then gives each match the mean starter score per side (h_fatigue, a_fatigue), the starters' summed 7-day minutes, and fatigue_diff. A side with no recorded starters gets nulls.

Note

Understat covers league matches only, so player rest is overstated for clubs that also play cups or European games. The schedule features below cover that gap at team level.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
club_calendar builds every club's full calendar from Transfermarkt (match_leagues, all competitions), and team_schedule_features attaches it to each Understat match as h_* and a_* columns:

  • rest_days_all: days since the previous game in any competition, capped at 30. A club's first game in the data has no previous one and gets 30.
  • games_7d_all, games_14d_all: games in the previous 7 and 14 days.
  • non_league_14d: cup, European or other games in the previous 14 days.
  • prev_europe_away: the previous game was an away European tie.
  • days_to_next_all, next_is_europe: look-ahead features, from fixtures already scheduled. days_to_next_all uses the date the next game was actually played, which for a postponed game was not known at kick-off.

A side whose club has no matched Transfermarkt game gets nulls.

docs.title: Players
docs.text:
get_player_features gives each starter a form line and spreads the eleven starters of each side into slot columns, ordered by line-up position from the goalkeeper forward. For each side (h, a), slot (1 to 11) and feature, the column is <side>_player<slot>_<feature>, for example h_player1_xg90:

Feature Meaning xg90, xa90 xG and xA per 90 minutes over the player's previous 10 matches form90 xG plus xA per 90 over the same window: expected goal involvement prev_min Minutes played over the same window fatigue_score The player's fatigue score (see Fatigue)

That makes 110 columns. Per-90 rates are null below 270 previous minutes, so a newcomer's numbers are not noise.

docs.title: Join
docs.text: join_features left-joins Elo, fatigue, schedule and the player slots onto cleaned_matches, one to one, so every match keeps its row. Elo has no game_id, so it joins on the match date and both teams. A feature is null where its source has no value for the game; missing.csv says why (see Missing values). The result is match_features.csv, the modelling table.

docs.title: Missing values
docs.text:
match_features.csv keeps its nulls and gains no columns for them. Instead missing_table writes missing.csv, a table of its own with one row per null cell: the match (game_id), the column, the side (h, a, or null for a column of the whole match) and the reason:

Reason Null cells no_lineup A side's fatigue and player slots, when Understat has no starters for it short_lineup A player slot left empty, when fewer than 11 starters are recorded too_few_minutes A starter's xg90, xa90 and form90, under 270 previous minutes no_schedule A side's schedule features, when its club has no Transfermarkt game no_next_game days_to_next_all, for a club's last game in the Transfermarkt data no_tm_game The Transfermarkt columns, when the match has no Transfermarkt game no_formation A side's formation columns, when its Transfermarkt game has no line-up plain_shape home_variant / away_variant, for a shape with no variant such as "4-2-3-1" other None of these, such as a formation that did not parse

Every null cell of match_features.csv has exactly one row, so the two tables always agree. The nulls stay null. Filling them with a mean or median of the table would leak later seasons into earlier ones, and a constant such as 0 would read as a real value: a newcomer is not a player with no expected goals. Gradient-boosted trees, as in feature_importance, take nulls as they are; a model that cannot should fill them inside its own training fold, and can join missing.csv to know why.

The one gap filled at the source is rest_days_all for a club's first game, which gets the 30-day cap, since the cap already means "a month or more".

docs.title: Model frame
docs.text:
model_frame.csv is match_features.csv with the gaps whose meaning is known handled, so a model can read it as it is. match_features.csv itself stays as it was. Each step answers one reason, as checked on the real data:

Reason In model_frame.csv no_lineup The match is dropped: two matches with no starters on either side no_formation The team's formation from its previous match, with h_formation_imputed / a_formation_imputed set; null if the team has none earlier. Most are La Liga 2018/19's first rounds no_next_game days_to_next_all = 30, the cap: the club's last game before the summer break plain_shape home_variant / away_variant = "none" too_few_minutes, short_lineup Kept null

The first season (2014/15) is dropped last, as warm-up: every player and team starts with no history, and about 18% of its starter slots are too_few_minutes, against 3-8% later. The formation fill runs before, so 2015/16 can use it. It only looks back: a team's most common formation would read its later games.

uv run clean_data ends by printing reason_counts(missing): the null cells and the matches they touch, per reason. null_report counts nulls per feature group instead:

import polars as pl
from money_printer_research.features import null_report, reason_counts

missing = pl.read_csv("data/clean/missing.csv")
print(reason_counts(missing))

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Every frame the pipeline reads or writes has a pandera model in money_printer_research.schema, with each column's dtype, checks and a description. The models are grouped by entity, the thing one row describes:

Entity One row per Page Match Match Match Player Player per match Player Club Club, or club per game Club Competition Transfermarkt competition Competition Bet Backtested game, or season of a strategy Bet

Inside each entity there is one module per pipeline stage, in order. An entity has only the stages it needs.

Module Holds raw.py Every column of a collected file, as the source names it. Collection checks every column, so a source that changes shape fails at download time. selected.py Only the raw columns the clean step reads, each copied from raw.py with the same type and description. clean.py The cleaned tables written as CSV. features.py The pre-match features built from the clean tables.

Everything is re-exported from the package, so any model can be imported as:

from money_printer_research.schema import CleanedMatchCols, PlayerStatCols

docs.title: Using a model in code
docs.text:
Every column is declared as a pandera FieldType, so a column name can be used directly in a polars expression and is typed as str:

import polars as pl
from money_printer_research.schema import ScheduleCols

played.filter(pl.col(ScheduleCols.season) == 1415)
